12205-lawyer-quince-odd-craft-part-5.creator: W.W. Jacobs
12205-lawyer-quince-odd-craft-part-5.description: A book by W.W. Jacobs. I've got the right to keep him locked up there as long as I like. I say it's agin the law, but Hogg he says no. I say his folks would come and try to break open my stable, but Hogg says if they do I can have the law of 'em for damaging my property."

arxiv-2107-01788.title: Integrability of Conformal Loop Ensemble: Imaginary DOZZ Formula and Beyond
arxiv-2107-01788.creator: Morris Ang UC San Diego Gefei Cai Peking University Xin Sun Peking University Baojun Wu Peking University
arxiv-2107-01788.description: Abstract The scaling limit of the probability that n n points are on the same cluster for 2D critical percolation is believed to be governed by a conformal field theory (CFT). Although this is not fully understood, Delfino and Viti (2010) made a remarkable prediction on the exact value of a properly normalized three-point probability.

arxiv-2108-00335.title: Towards Adversarially Robust and Domain Generalizable Stereo Matching by Rethinking DNN Feature Backbones
arxiv-2108-00335.creator: Kelvin Cheng, Christopher Healey, Tianfu Wu
arxiv-2108-00335.description: Abstract Stereo matching has recently witnessed remarkable progress using Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). But, how robust are they? Although it has been well-known that DNNs often suffer from adversarial vulnerability with a catastrophic drop in performance, the situation is even worse in stereo matching. This paper first shows that a type of weak white-box attacks can overwhelm state-of-the-art methods.

arxiv-2111-01125.title: U q ​ ( s ​ l ​ ( 2 ) ) U_{q}(sl(2)) -quantum invariants from an intersection of two Lagrangians in a symmetric power of a surface
arxiv-2111-01125.creator: Cristina Anghel, / ⁣ / /\!\!/, 13 th May 2022
arxiv-2111-01125.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Cristina Anghel, / ⁣ / /\!\!/, 13 th May 2022. In this paper we show that coloured Jones and coloured Alexander polynomials can both be read off from the same picture provided by two Lagrangians in a symmetric power of a surface. More specifically, the N t ​ h N^{th} coloured Jones and N t ​ h N^{th} coloured Alexander polynomials are specialisations of a graded intersection between two explicit Lagrangian submanifolds in a symmetric power of the punctured disc.

arxiv-2210-00890.title: Evolutionary status of selected post-AGB stars based on Gaia DR3
arxiv-2210-00890.creator: M. Parthasarathy, Marina Kounkel, Keivan G. Stassun
arxiv-2210-00890.description: Abstract The evolutionary status of 24 post-AGB stars is presented based on Gaia DR3 data. All 24 stars have parallaxes accurate to better than 3 ​ σ 3\sigma and have RUWE values < 1.4 <1.4 . Based on the Gaia DR3 distances the absolute luminosities are derived. For 14 of the stars, the luminosities confirm their post-AGB evolutionary stage.

arxiv-2210-13120.title: Axion-Photon Conversion of LHAASO Multi-TeV and PeV Photons
arxiv-2210-13120.creator: Guangshuai Zhang (张光帅) 1, Bo-Qiang Ma (马伯强) 1,2,3
arxiv-2210-13120.description: Abstract The Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) has reported the detection of a large number of multi-TeV-scale photon events including also several PeV-scale gamma-ray-photon events with energy as high as 1.4 PeV. The possibility that some of these events may have extragalactic origins is not yet excluded.

arxiv-2303-15619.title: Typhoon: Gradient-Based Task-Specific Masking for Masked Language Models
arxiv-2303-15619.creator: Bruce Changlong Xu, Muhammed Shahir Abdurrahman, Hashem Elezabi
arxiv-2303-15619.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Bruce Changlong Xu, Muhammed Shahir Abdurrahman, Hashem Elezabi. The choice of which tokens to mask is an under-examined design decision in masked language modeling (MLM). Standard pretraining masks tokens uniformly at random, whereas content-aware masking schemes can improve downstream transfer. We study masking as a task-adaptive component of the fine-tuning pipeline and introduce Typhoon , a masking strategy that uses the gradient of the MLM loss with respect to one-hot token inputs to estimate online how much each token type contributes to the objective.

arxiv-2304-00467.title: Robust Multiview Point Cloud Registration with Reliable Pose Graph Initialization and History Reweighting
arxiv-2304-00467.creator: Haiping WangWuhan University, Yuan LiuThe University of Hong KongZhen DongWuhan UniversityYulan GuoSun Yat-sen UniversityYu-Shen LiuTsinghua UniversityWenping WangTexas A&M University, Bisheng YangWuhan University
arxiv-2304-00467.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a new method for the multiview registration of point cloud. Previous multiview registration methods rely on exhaustive pairwise registration to construct a densely-connected pose graph and apply Iteratively Reweighted Least Square (IRLS) on the pose graph to compute the scan poses.

arxiv-2304-02155.title: Cat-qubit-inspired gate on cos( 2 ​ θ 2\theta ) qubits
arxiv-2304-02155.creator: Catherine Leroux, Alexandre Blais
arxiv-2304-02155.description: Abstract For cos ⁡ ( 2 ​ θ ) \cos(2\theta) qubits based on voltage-controlled semiconductor nanowire Josephson junctions we introduce a single-qubit Z Z gate inspired by the noise-bias preserving gate of the Kerr-cat qubit. This scheme relies on a π \pi rotation in phase space via a beamsplitter-like transformation between a qubit and ancilla qubit.

arxiv-2304-05741.title: Learning to search for and detect objects in foveal images using deep learning
arxiv-2304-05741.creator: Beatriz Paula, Plinio Moreno
arxiv-2304-05741.description: Abstract The human visual system processes images with varied degrees of resolution, with the fovea, a small portion of the retina, capturing the highest acuity region, which gradually declines toward the field of view’s periphery. However, the majority of existing object localization methods rely on images acquired by image sensors with space-invariant resolution, ignoring biological attention mechanisms.

arxiv-2305-04093.title: An improved regret analysis for UCB-N and TS-N
arxiv-2305-04093.creator: Nishant A. Mehta
arxiv-2305-04093.description: Abstract In the setting of stochastic online learning with undirected feedback graphs, Lykouris et al. 2020 previously analyzed the pseudo-regret of the upper confidence bound-based algorithm UCB-N and the Thompson Sampling-based algorithm TS-N. In this note, we show how to improve their pseudo-regret analysis.

arxiv-2310-01579.title: Titration in Canonical and Grand-Canonical Ensembles
arxiv-2310-01579.creator: Amin Bakhshandeh, Yan Levin
arxiv-2310-01579.description: Abstract We discuss problems associated with the notion of pH in heterogeneous systems. For homogeneous systems, standardization protocols lead to a well defined quantity, which although different from Sørensen’s original idea of pH, is well reproducible and has become accepted as the measure of the “hydrogen potential”.

arxiv-2403-04715.description: Abstract Molecular emission is used to investigate both the physical and chemical properties of protoplanetary disks. Therefore, to accurately derive disk properties, we need a thorough understanding of the behavior of the molecular probes we rely on. Here we investigate how the molecular line emission of N 2 H + \!

arxiv-2409-13924.title: A coherent approach to quantum-classical optimization
arxiv-2409-13924.creator: Authors: Andrés N. Cáliz 1 Jordi Riu 1,2 , Josep Bosch 1 , Pau Torrente 1 , Jose Miralles 1 , Arnau Riera 1
arxiv-2409-13924.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Authors: Andrés N. Cáliz 1 Jordi Riu 1,2 , Josep Bosch 1 , Pau Torrente 1 , Jose Miralles 1 , Arnau Riera 1. Hybrid quantum-classical optimization techniques, which incorporate the pre-optimization of Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) using Tensor Networks (TNs), have been shown to allow for the reduction of quantum computational resources.

arxiv-2502-08957.title: Training Trajectory Predictors Without Ground-Truth Data
arxiv-2502-08957.creator: Mikolaj Kliniewski *, Jesse Morris, Ian R. Manchester, and Viorela Ila
arxiv-2502-08957.description: Abstract This paper presents a framework capable of accurately and smoothly estimating position, heading, and velocity. Using this high-quality input, we propose a system based on Trajectron++ [ 1 ] , able to consistently generate precise trajectory predictions. Unlike conventional models that require ground-truth data for training, our approach eliminates this dependency.

arxiv-2505-18418.title: McARL:Morphology-Control-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Generalizable Quadrupedal Locomotion
arxiv-2505-18418.creator: Prakhar Mishra, Amir Hossain Raj, Xuesu Xiao, Dinesh Manocha
arxiv-2505-18418.description: Abstract We present Morphology-Control-Aware Reinforcement Learning (McARL), a new approach to overcome challenges of hyperparameter tuning and transfer loss, that enables generalizable locomotion across robot morphologies. We use a morphology conditioned policy by incorporating a randomized morphological vector, sampled from the defined morphology range, into both the actor and critic.

arxiv-2602-06905.creator: Watse Sybesma ∗ and, Poula Tadros ∗,†
arxiv-2602-06905.description: Abstract We present new black hole solutions to the low-energy effective action of string theory. We introduce three- and four-dimensional solutions that are rotating, asymptotically flat, and exhibit a linear dilaton vacuum. pmc-10737056.title: FUNCTIONAL LIMITATIONS, LIVING ARRANGEMENT, DAILY SOCIAL CONTACTS, AND LONELINESS IN LATE LIFE
pmc-10737056.creator: Shiyang Zhang
pmc-10737056.description: Older adults with functional limitations are at a greater risk of social isolation and loneliness, largely due to difficulties in mobility and compromised social contacts. Lack of social contact throughout the day may contribute to loneliness among older adults with functional limitations, and these associations may differ by living arrangements.

pmc-11369708.title: Comparison of executive functions in Russian and Japanese preschoolers
pmc-11369708.creator: Aleksander Veraksa, Mari Hasegawa, Daria Bukhalenkova, Olga Almazova, Margarita Aslanova, Emi Matsumoto
pmc-11369708.description: This study analyzed differences in level of main executive function (EF) components (such as inhibition, working memory, and cognitive flexibility) among Russian and Japanese preschoolers. The study involved 102 children of 5–6.9 years old: 51 child from Russia and 51 child from Japan. Out of 102 children 48 were boys and 54 girls.

pmc-11488850.title: The ketone body β-hydroxybutyrate ameliorates neurodevelopmental deficits in the GABAergic system of daf-18/PTEN Caenorhabditis elegans mutants
pmc-11488850.creator: Sebastián Giunti, María Gabriela Blanco, María José De Rosa, Diego Rayes, K VijayRaghavan, Sebastian Giunti, Maria Gabriela Blanco, Maria Jose De Rosa, Diego Rayes
pmc-11488850.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A finely tuned balance between excitation and inhibition (E/I) is essential for proper brain function. Disruptions in the GABAergic system, which alter this equilibrium, are a common feature in various types of neurological disorders, including autism spectrum disorders (ASDs). Mutations in Phosphatase and Tensin Homolog (PTEN), the main negative regulator of the phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate kinase/Akt pathway, are strongly associated with ASD. However, it is unclear whether PTEN deficiencies can differentially affect inhibitory and excitatory signaling.

pmc-11652367.title: Integrative analysis of PANoptosis-related genes in diabetic retinopathy: machine learning identification and experimental validation
pmc-11652367.creator: Han Chen, Enguang Chen, Ting Cao, Feifan Feng, Min Lin, Xuan Wang, Yu Xu
pmc-11652367.description: BackgroundDiabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major complication of diabetes, leading to severe vision impairment. Understanding the molecular mechanisms, particularly PANoptosis, underlying DR is crucial for identifying potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This study aims to identify differentially expressed PANoptosis-related genes (DE-PRGs) in DR, offering insights into the disease’s pathogenesis and potential diagnostic tools.

pmc-11659241.title: Psychometric properties of the pain anxiety symptom scale among postoperative patients in Amol, Iran
pmc-11659241.creator: Hamid Sharif-Nia, Erika Sivarajan Froelicher, João Marôco, Esmaeil Hoseinzadeh, Sima Hejazi, Reza Fatehi, Poorya Nowrozi, Bita Mohammadi
pmc-11659241.description: IntroductionSo far, the psychometric properties of the Persian version of the Pain Anxiety Symptom Scale have not been assessed in Iran. Therefore, this study was conducted to determine the validity and reliability of the Persian version of the Pain Anxiety Symptom Scale among a group of Iranian patients in Amol.

pmc-11733963.title: Hemangioma of the Mitral Valve and Aortomitral Curtain in an Adolescent
pmc-11733963.creator: Aditya Sengupta, Gina LaRocca, Martin E. Goldman, David H. Adams, Anelechi C. Anyanwu
pmc-11733963.description: A hemangioma of the mitral valve and aortomitral curtain was incidentally discovered in an adolescent. The lesion was surgically excised, and the mitral valve was reconstructed with complete preservation of valvular function. Pertinent principles of multimodality imaging-based diagnosis and nuances of operative management of this rare, vascular tumor are discussed.

pmc-12401007.title: Construction and optimization of a nisin-controlled expression vector using a pre-screened strong promoter in Streptococcus thermophilus
pmc-12401007.creator: Yanxin Ye, Ruiting Zhao, Leilei Li, Zhi Li, Yanyan Chen, Zhenshang Xu
pmc-12401007.description: The nisin-controlled gene expression (NICE) system is an efficient and promising gene expression system for Lactococcus lactis. To enhance the expression efficiency of the NICE system in Streptococcus thermophilus ATCC19258, an inducible expression vector, pNZ8148-PnisA-gfp-PnisR-nisR-nisK, containing the regulatory element NisR/K and the promoter PnisR, was first constructed using the basic plasmid pNZ8148.

pmc-12558594.title: PROTOCOL: The Effects of Land Management Policies on the Environment and People in Low‐ and Middle‐Income Countries: A Systematic Review
pmc-12558594.creator: Pierre Marion, Ingunn Storhaug, Sanghwa Lee, Claudia Romero, Constanza Gonzalez Parrao, Birte Snilstveit
pmc-12558594.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Addressing the climate change and biodiversity loss crises while ensuring livelihoods are not negatively affected is a matter that requires urgent action. A recently published Evidence Gap Map (EGM) identified no recent systematic reviews on land management interventions. Drawing from this EGM, the review aims to examine and synthesise the latest evidence on what works, how, and at what cost to improve environmental and human welfare outcomes in land management in low‐ and middle‐income countries.

pmc-12610397.title: Early structural valve deterioration of a pulmonary position Inspiris Resilia valve requiring redo pulmonary and tricuspid valve replacement
pmc-12610397.creator: Akito Inoue, Ryohei Ushioda, Hidenobu Akamatsu, Tasuku Kawarabayashi, Jeonga Lee, Jun Maruoka, Kentaro Shirakura, Yuki Setogawa, Ryo Okubo, Hiroyuki Miyamoto, Aina Hirofuji, Shogo Takahashi, Daisuke Takeyoshi, Shingo Kunioka, Hiroyuki Kamiya
pmc-12610397.description: We report a 50-year-old woman with pulmonary and tricuspid valve regurgitation who required redo pulmonary and tricuspid valve replacement (PVR, TVR). At age 8, she underwent right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction for pulmonary stenosis, and at 44 years she had PVR with a 19 mm Inspiris Resilia bioprosthesis and tricuspid annuloplasty with a 28 mm Physio ring.

pmc-13409954.title: Arrhythmias in Autoimmune Diseases: Immune-Mediated Mechanisms and Management
pmc-13409954.creator: Kamala P. Tamirisa, Jorge A. Irizarry-Caro, Ian Curnutt, Devika Adusumilli, Mia Jose, Meenakshi Jolly, Estelle Torbey, Annabelle S. Volgman

pmc-13645743.title: A multiparty homomorphic encryption approach to confidential federated Kaplan–Meier survival analysis
pmc-13645743.creator: Narasimha Raghavan Veeraragavan, Svetlana Boudko, Jan Franz Nygård
pmc-13645743.description: The proliferation of real-world health data enables multi-institutional survival studies, yet privacy constraints preclude centralizing sensitive records. We present a privacy-preserving federated Kaplan–Meier framework based on threshold CKKS (Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song) homomorphic encryption that supports approximate floating-point computation and encrypted aggregation of per-time-point counts while exposing only public outputs.

uslaw-cfr-t20-s220-170.title: 20 C.F.R. § 220.170 — The trial work period.
uslaw-cfr-t20-s220-170.creator: Railroad Retirement Board
uslaw-cfr-t20-s220-170.description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 20 (Employees' Benefits), Part 220 (Determining Disability). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). (a) Definition of the trial work period. The trial work period is a period during which the annuitant may test his or her ability to work and still be considered disabled. The trial work period begins and ends as described in paragraph (e).

The purpose of this standard is to insure safe braking performance under normal and emergency conditions. S3. Application. This standard applies.
